body:
Replacement coils and pods are the most common reason for a wrong-part order. They look similar across brands, and even across models of the same brand, but fitments differ. Ordering the wrong part wastes money and leaves you without a working device. This guide explains how to identify your device, how to read compatibility lists, how to match resistance and liquid type, how to buy spares, how to avoid counterfeit parts, how to fit and prime a new part, how to know when to replace and what to do when you are stuck. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## Start with your device name
Find the exact model on the device or box, not just the brand. Many brands make a dozen pod systems that all use different pods. The model name is often printed on the base, on the box or on the maker's website. If you only know the brand, take a clear photo of the device, including any markings, and send it to us. A wrong guess is the commonest mistake.

## Check the series
Coil and pod listings usually name compatible devices. In our [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) category, each product states what it fits. If your device is not listed, do not guess. Compatibility lists are written by the maker, and they are the reference. A part that fits physically may not suit the electronics, and a part that looks identical may differ in coil resistance or in how it seals.

## Know what you are buying
- **Pod:** the container, which may include the coil. Pre-filled pods are replaced whole.
- **Coil head:** the replaceable heating part that screws into a tank or pod.
- **Cartridge:** a term used for a pre-filled pod or a replaceable unit, depending on the brand.
- **Tank:** a refillable container, usually with a replaceable coil.

If the listing is unclear about what is included, ask us.

## Match the resistance
Coils list a resistance in ohms. Lower resistance means more power and more vapor, higher resistance suits tighter draws. Use the resistance your device was designed for. Our guide to [sub-ohm versus mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/) explains the difference. A coil outside your device's range can perform badly or be unsuitable. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Pick the liquid type
Some coils suit thicker liquid and higher power, others suit thin salt-based liquid. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Using the wrong liquid can cause leaks or burnt tastes. If the coil's packaging recommends a liquid type, follow it.

## Coil material and type
Most modern replacement coils are mesh. Others use wire or ceramic. Mesh coils tend to give smooth flavor; see [what is a mesh coil](/blog/what-is-a-mesh-coil/) and [mesh vs standard coils](/blog/dual-mesh-vs-single-mesh-coils/). Choose the type your device is designed for, and do not try to adapt a coil of a different design.

## Buy a spare
Keep one spare on hand so a worn coil does not leave you without a working device. Learn [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). Packs of several coils usually cost less per coil. Store spares in their packaging, upright, in a cool, dry place away from children and pets.

## Fitting a new coil or pod
1. Switch the device off and remove the old part.
2. Check the contacts are clean and dry.
3. Unpack the new part and avoid touching the cotton.
4. Prime the coil by adding a few drops of liquid. See [how to prime a new coil or pod](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/).
5. Seat the part firmly.
6. Fill with liquid below the line, and let it rest for five to ten minutes.
7. Start at low power, with gentle puffs.

## Avoid counterfeit parts
Buy from a reputable seller. Poorly made coils can taste burnt, fail early or fit badly. Compare the packaging with the maker's images, check for the correct model and look for batch codes. See [how to spot counterfeit vapes](/blog/how-to-spot-counterfeit-vapes/). A coil that is much cheaper than usual may be old or fake.

## When to replace
Replace a coil or pod when flavor fades, vapor thins or a burnt taste appears. Do not wait until it is dry. As a rough guide, coils last from several days to a few weeks, depending on use, liquid and power. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/).

## A worked example
You have a pod system called "Model X" from a brand that also makes "Model X2". The pods look the same, but the listing for Model X pods says it fits Model X only. You check the base of your device, which reads "X". You buy a pack of two pods for $8. You also buy a spare pack, so that you always have one. When the first pod's flavor fades after ten days, you swap in a new one, prime it and carry on. If you had bought X2 pods by mistake, they might not have fitted, and you would have lost days.

## When you are stuck
Send us the model name and a photo through the [contact page](/contact/) and we will point you to the right part. Include any markings on the device, and the listing you are considering. Adults 21+ only.

## Common mistakes
- **Ordering by brand alone.**
- **Assuming similar-looking pods are compatible.**
- **Ignoring resistance.**
- **Forgetting to prime.**
- **Buying the cheapest unknown part.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I use pods from another brand?
Usually not. Pods are designed for specific devices.

### What if my device is discontinued?
Pods may become hard to find. Consider a newer device with widely available parts.

### How many coils should I buy?
A pack of several, so you always have a spare.

### Can I clean and reuse a coil?
Not reliably. Replace it.

### Do coils expire?
They keep well in their packaging, but use them within a reasonable time.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Frequently asked questions about parts
### What is the difference between a coil and a pod?
A pod is a container, and in many devices it contains the coil. A coil head is a replaceable heating part that fits into a tank or pod.

### Why is my new coil not working?
Check that it matches the device, that it is seated firmly and that the contacts are clean. Prime it, and let it soak. If it still fails, contact us.

### How do I know the resistance of my device's coil?
It is printed on the coil, or listed in the specifications. Many devices show it on screen.

### Can I mix coil brands in one tank?
Only if the tank is designed for it. Check the maker's list.

### How do I store spare parts?
Upright, in their packaging, in a cool, dry place away from children and pets.

## A routine for replacing parts
Check flavor each day. When it fades, swap in a spare. Prime it, fill, rest and use. Order a new spare the same day. Write the date on the box. This simple routine means you never run out, and your device always works at its best.

## Cost of parts over a year
A pod or coil at about $4 for two, replaced every two weeks, costs about $52 a year. A pack of five coils at $10, replaced weekly, costs about $104 a year. Add liquid, and you have the running cost of the device. Compare that with disposables for your own use, and decide which suits you.

## More help with choosing parts
### A note on resistance ranges
Many pod coils are around 0.6 to 1.2 ohms, and tank coils range from about 0.15 to 1.5 ohms. Your device's manual shows the range it supports. Do not use a coil outside it.

### A note on pod capacity
Most pods hold about 2 mL. A larger pod holds more but may not fit your device. Match the capacity the maker lists.

### A note on color and labeling
Some makers color-code coils by resistance. Check the listing, and do not rely on color alone.

### What to do with old parts
Take finished pods and coils to a recycling site, with your devices. See [how to dispose of vapes and batteries](/blog/how-to-dispose-of-vapes-and-batteries/). Keep old parts away from children and pets.

### Keeping a parts list
Write down your device model, the part names and the sizes you buy, in a note on your phone. Next time, you can order in a minute. If you have more than one device, keep a list for each.

## A short summary
Identify your device by its exact model, find a part that lists it as compatible, check the resistance and liquid type, buy a spare and prime each new part. If you are stuck, send us the model and a photo. Following that sequence prevents nearly all wrong-part orders, and it keeps your device working as the maker intended. Keep your parts list up to date, and replace parts on time.

## When a part is out of stock
If the part you need is unavailable, do not substitute a different one. Contact us and we will tell you whether it is expected back, or suggest a compatible alternative. A wrong part is worse than a short wait.
